_comment: Source of truth for the Ticket Fund project list. Derived 2026-09-15 from applications/art/grant-budget-v2.md (submission draft, sections A-D + camp-funded), applications/art/itemized-budget.md (for projects cut from the grant but still planned), camp/finances.md (fuel) and projects/*/README.md (descriptions). Project ids are stable slugs so seed.mjs can be re-run safely. Costs are the grant-listed retail estimates; real costs run lower via hookups (camp/finances.md).

projects.name: Logistics
projects.description:
Getting everything to Virginia Key and back. Box truck for build week, trailer for the Speeder and oversize pieces, pallet delivery, fuel. Not glamorous, not optional — this comes off the top of the budget before any art is funded.

Source: applications/art/grant-budget-v2.md section D (fuel from camp/finances.md — real cost, not grantable).

items.name: 16-ft box truck rental (build week, 5 days + mileage)

projects.name: Camp Infrastructure
projects.description:
The dues-funded basics that make the camp run: power safety, the kitchen food-call bell/clock, consumables, and a contingency cushion. Also hosts the now-playing screens and event bus (hardware already owned by Ben, so $0 here).

Source: applications/art/grant-budget-v2.md 'Camp-funded (dues, NOT in grant)'; projects/kitchen-clock/README.md; projects/now-playing-screens/README.md.

items.name: Kitchen clock + food-call bell (bell, solenoid, button, ESP32/PSU)
Consumables: fog fluid, gaff, zip ties, velcro
Now-playing screens + event bus (Pi, touchscreen, router — owned by Ben)

projects.name: Projection Cube Green Room
projects.description:
The anchor build: an insulated freestanding ~12x16 room whose exterior walls are a projection-mapped video canvas (mapped from inside the tent), while the interior is the performers' prep and decompression space — the Green Room. Art on the outside, function on the inside: mirrors, makeup-grade lighting, greenery, rugs and cushions, a mending nook.

Source: applications/art/grant-budget-v2.md section A; projects/green-room/README.md; applications/art/green-room-draft.md.

items.name: Ratchet straps + 4 heavy lag ground anchors

projects.name: Pallet Dance Floor
projects.description:
Rain-proof raised pallet floor for the dance area and performance ground (16x20), Burning Man standard. Pallets purchased (rentals aren't grantable) and delivered locally; plywood topper, carpets, edge ramps.

Source: applications/art/grant-budget-v2.md section B.

projects.name: Interactive Instrument Garden
projects.description:
All the capacitive/sensor art bundled as one interconnected installation — the SHOWTIME band and its companions. Touch, motion and sound feed a shared camp event bus so the pieces talk to each other: a staff cast ripples the crystals, a painting touch surges the tunnel, an altar crescendo lights everything. The shared electronics, LEDs and finish materials live here; each piece is a sub-project with its own vote.

Source: applications/art/grant-budget-v2.md section C.

items.name: Sensor/LED controllers, boards, wiring, PSUs (all pieces)
Paint, deco, finish materials across all pieces

projects.name: SHOWTIME Band (touch instruments)
projects.description:
The playable instruments of the garden: water-cylinder chord tubes, a mancala drum-sequencer board, a conductor's podium, and a mushroom drum kit — capacitive and piezo sensors on a Pi/ESP32 driving sound and light. Instruments on pedestals people can walk up and play together.

Source: grant-budget-v2 section C; projects/touch-sound-light/README.md.

items.name: Water-cylinder chord tubes (acrylic tubes, basins, seals, LED bases)
Conductor podium build (lumber, panel, knob plate)
Mushroom drum kit (sculpt foam, coating, piezo triggers)

projects.name: Magic Crystals ×40
projects.description:
Cheap, scatterable glowing crystals that are networked effect nodes — they listen for commands from the other art (staff casts, audio-bus beats, altar crescendos, puzzle wins) and respond with light. No network? They fall back to a self-contained auto mode and just be pretty. Resin/PETG shells, ESP32-C3, LED rings, cells and chargers.

Source: grant-budget-v2 section C; projects/magic-crystals/README.md.

items.name: Magic crystal (resin, PETG shell, ESP32-C3, LEDs, cell, charger)

projects.name: Intentions Altar
projects.description:
An altar of stones and light. Take a stone, speak your intention, place the stone on the altar — the altar responds with light. Optionally a microphone hears the intention and the response matches its mood; stones placed back-to-back build escalating intensity. Sculpted structure, stones, fog burst, DMX wash finale.

Source: grant-budget-v2 section C; projects/intentions-altar/README.md.

items.name: Intentions altar (structure lumber, sculpt, stones, finish)

projects.name: Flow Toys: Magic Staff, Gada, Nunchucks, Hoops
projects.description:
Carryable props with motion sensors (IMU) driving their own lights and sounds — swing it, spin it, slam it, and it responds. Stretch goal: the staff casts at camp installations — gestures trigger effects on the tunnel, altar and crystals over the camp network. Polycarb tubes, printed cores, 18650 packs.

Source: grant-budget-v2 section C; projects/magic-staff/README.md.

items.name: Flow toy cores + hoops (polycarb, tubing, fasteners, electronics)

projects.name: Capacitive Touch Paintings ×6
projects.description:
Actual paintings that are secretly controllers. Conductive paint worked into the artwork creates touch zones — touch the moon in the painting and something happens: sound, light, the crystals ripple, the tunnel surges. Art you're supposed to touch.

Source: grant-budget-v2 section C; projects/touch-paintings/README.md.

items.name: Touch painting (conductive paint, canvas, sealant, ESP32)

projects.name: Smirkle Furniture (bass-shaker lounge)
projects.description:
Flat-pack plywood lounge furniture with bass-shaker transducers built in — you feel the music through the seat. A camp member's 4 shakers + Dayton amp cover half the transducers in-kind.

Source: grant-budget-v2 section C; camp/finances.md ledger.

items.name: Smirkle furniture: flat-pack plywood lounge builds

projects.name: Spinning Shadow-Lamp Polyhedra
projects.description:
Motorised polyhedral lamps on slip rings throwing moving geometric shadows across the camp — RGBW inside, cut-out plastics outside. Trim-ladder candidate (prototype-only saves ~$200).

Source: grant-budget-v2 section C.

items.name: Shadow-lamp polyhedra (slip rings, mounts, plastics, RGBW)

projects.name: Aerial Swing
projects.description:
A rig-hung swing for participants between aerial performances — the rig earns its keep all day. Rigger has veto on everything that touches the load path.

Source: grant-budget-v2 section C; safety rules in projects/aerial-rig-motion/README.md.

projects.name: Speeder Art Car Lighting Refresh
projects.description:
New strips, wiring and a topper for the Speeder art car so it reads as part of the SHOWTIME camp at night. Trim-ladder candidate (self-fund saves $270).

Source: grant-budget-v2 section C.

projects.name: Aerial Shadow Play
projects.description:
Three colored lights on a sliding motorised track behind the aerialist, casting overlapping shadows onto a backdrop. Converge the lights → one crisp silhouette. Diverge them → the performer splits into three colored shadows that drift, mix and blend. Not in the grant v2 ask — vote decides whether it happens.

Source: applications/art/itemized-budget.md; projects/aerial-shadow-play/README.md.

projects.name: Motion-Sensing Aerial Rig
projects.description:
An IMU on the aerial apparatus (and/or the performer) so movement drives the show — spins become color sweeps, swings push waves of light, a big drop hits like a bass note. Clamp-on only, nothing enters the load path, rigger has veto. Plus uplighting for the rig itself. Not in the grant v2 ask.

Source: applications/art/itemized-budget.md; projects/aerial-rig-motion/README.md.

projects.name: Auto-Resetting Puzzles ×3
projects.description:
Physical puzzles that reset themselves — no camp member needed to re-arm them. Walk up, solve, get a satisfying payoff (light, sound, a crystal ripple), and it's instantly ready for the next person. RFID/NFC readers, ESP32, printed parts. Not in the grant v2 ask.

Source: applications/art/itemized-budget.md; projects/auto-reset-puzzles/README.md.

items.name: Puzzle unit (RC522 readers ×4, ESP32, LEDs, DFPlayer + speaker, NFC tags, filament)

projects.name: Frontage Marquee Sign
projects.description:
The camp name in cabaret bulbs across the frontage — SHOWTIME literalism, pure curb appeal. Plywood letters, S14 LED bulb strings, a dimmer. Not in the grant v2 ask.

Source: applications/art/itemized-budget.md; applications/art/budget.md Scenario B.

projects.name: Space Hallway LED Re-skin
projects.description:
The LED tunnel (Pixelblaze-driven) returns for 2027 as in-kind art regardless. This project is the optional full re-skin: all strips new, diffusers, a spare controller — plus the planned upgrades (setup markings, 3D LED mapping, AI-assisted effect workflow) that cost labor, not money. Not in the grant v2 ask.

Source: applications/art/itemized-budget.md; projects/space-hallway/README.md.

projects.name: CNC Projection Art
projects.description:
Layered CNC-cut plywood pieces hung in a tent corner and projection-mapped — dimensional surfaces the projectors paint. A camp member designs and cuts them on a CNC. Final form still open: corner piece, backlit obelisk, or sound-system facade totems. Projectors are in-kind. Approved in the 9/14 grant-bundle discussion; not in the grant v2 ask.

Source: applications/art/itemized-budget.md 'Projection surfaces'; projects/cnc-projection-art/README.md.

projects.name: Input Toys ×5
projects.description:
Small, sturdy, irresistible physical inputs scattered around camp — big buttons, cranks, sliders, levers — that do nothing locally except feel great, and publish everything they sense to the camp event bus. What each toy controls is a mapping decision, changeable any time. Not in the grant v2 ask.

Source: applications/art/itemized-budget.md; projects/input-toys/README.md.

items.name: Input toy (arcade button / encoder crank / lever + ESP32 + enclosure)
